normalized.governing_thought: Yes, raise prices in 2027 — but by segment: mid-market and enterprise from January, SMB only after a test
executive_summary: Churn is rising in one place: SMB monthly logo churn rose 2.0% → 3.1%; mid-market 0.6% → 0.8%; enterprise flat at 0.2%. Within SMB, the 2025 50%-off promotion cohort explains ~90% of the increase. Other SMB customers: 2.0% → 2.1%.

Price matters — but not where the CFO plan applies it hardest: Core SMB churners cite price no more than in 2025 (18% vs 19%). But promo churners do (52%) after their discount ended, and Inkwell’s $9 Starter has cut our contested SMB win rate from 51% to 38%.

$10.3M is a headline, not a 2027 number: 12% × all ARR ignores renewal timing and enterprise caps: only $7.6M is capturable in 2027, and an SMB churn response cuts that to ~$5.0–6.3M, losing ~320–640 SMB customers.

Recommendation: Mid-market +10% at renewal ($3.5M) · Enterprise to contract terms — 7% where capped, 10% otherwise ($0.8M) · Hold SMB list prices in H1, run a controlled renewal test and an activation programme. = $4.3M, up to ~$5.1M if the April/July checkpoints pass.
What it delivers: If segments repeat trailing NRR, ARR reaches ~$98.3M (+14.2%); the 15% goal ($98.9M) needs ≥$0.7M new-logo ARR or the checkpoint upside. NRR stays ~114%, far above the 100% floor.

normalized.recommendation: Raise prices by segment: Mid-market +10% list price at renewal from January 2027 (+$3.5M run-rate); Enterprise raise at renewal to contract terms — 7% where capped, 10% otherwise (+$0.8M ceiling); SMB hold list prices in H1 2027, exclude the promo cohort from any 2027 rise, approve the +8% renewal test; fund the SMB activation programme without booking churn savings in the plan; Finance to define the board churn metric and provide a 2027 new-logo ARR forecast; confirm the April (mid-market) and July (SMB) checkpoints and their thresholds. = $4.3M, up to ~$5.1M if the April/July checkpoints pass.

alternatives_considered.option: A. CFO plan: +12% on every plan at renewal
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected. $10.3M headline shrinks to ~$5.0–6.3M once renewal timing, contract caps and SMB churn are counted; loses ~320–640 SMB customers. Main risk: SMB churn response unknown; feeds Inkwell; MM priced above tested level. A’s extra ARR is mostly the SMB rise, worth $0–1.3M net with downside, in the one segment where we lack evidence.

alternatives_considered.option: B. Segmented: MM +10%, Ent to terms, SMB hold + test
alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended. $4.3M (up to $5.1M via checkpoints); ARR $98.3M (+14.2%); NRR ~114%. Main risk: relies on new-logo ARR or checkpoint upside to clear 15%. Can recover most of A's extra by July once the test shows whether the risk is real.
Not chosen. $0 uplift; ARR $94.0M (+9.3%), needs $4.9M new-logo ARR; NRR ~109%. Main risk: misses growth goal; leaves MM/Ent value unused.
Mid-market set at +10% — the tested level — rather than the CFO’s 12%, with a step-up gate (step H2 renewals to 12% if repriced renewals churn ≤1.0%/mo at April checkpoint).
Described as a coin-flip that could net close to zero (net $1.25M under 2023 pattern, $0.02M under 2× stress); SMB instead held with a +8% controlled test.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Synthetic benchmark data from the internal briefing pack only; no external research.
All ARR effects are end-2027 run-rate; in-year revenue is lower because renewals fall through the year.
Enterprise 7% caps assumed spread evenly across renewing and non-renewing enterprise contracts.
Promo-cohort churn (~4.9%) is implied using mid-2026 counts, so it is approximate.
Activation decomposition (~0.8 of 2.8 pts) assumes the 3× ratio holds for all SMB; directional only.
SMB churn response scales the 2023 +8% pattern linearly with price; stress multiple (2×) is illustrative.
End-2027 ARR assumes each segment repeats its trailing-12-month NRR; new-logo ARR excluded because the pack has no forecast; each 1 pt of overall NRR ≈ $0.9M.
Enterprise $0.8M is a ceiling, not a forecast.
Checkpoint upside assumes renewals spread evenly over the year.
Uncertainty #1: whether core SMB is more price-sensitive since Inkwell — we cannot yet tell which SMB churn case applies.
Uncertainty #2: promo cohort may churn regardless.
Uncertainty #3: 2024 mid-market test covered new sign-ups only; existing mid-market may react worse at renewal.
Inkwell may move upmarket; we do not know how much of mid-market is 51–200 seats.
Renewal notice periods are not in the pack; adjust the January start if contracts require longer notice.
Board dashboard churn figure (1.4% → 2.3%) is undefined and cannot be reconciled with Table 1; set aside.
Customer Success claim to halve SMB churn within two quarters is not supported by the pack.
Checkpoint thresholds are proposals for leadership to confirm.
Data gaps: new-logo ARR forecast, renewal dates and notice periods, mid-market seat-size mix, SMB monthly vs annual split, exit-survey response rates.

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck gives its overall answer in two slide titles: slide 1, "Raise prices in 2027 where we have pricing power — and fix SMB before we reprice it", and slide 2, the executive summary, whose title I used as the governing thought. There were no images; all charts came as series data. For the waterfall charts on slides 9 and 12, I took the values from the data labels printed on each slide. The base, total, increase and decrease series are what drew the charts. Slide 8 says in its speaker notes that it uses colour shading, which the plain text does not show. Executive summary points combine each heading with its supporting sentence.
